title: A Person Through Other People
objective: After this level you can explain the southern African idea of ubuntu, that a person is a person through other persons, and how it challenges a purely individual self.
summary: Ubuntu holds that a person is a person through other persons; Menkiti said personhood is attained through communal life, and Eze defends the individual.

cards.headline: Can you be a person all by yourself?
cards.body: A southern African maxim answers no: umuntu ngumuntu ngabantu. Philosophers have built a whole view of the self on it.

cards.headline: A person through other persons
cards.body: The Zulu and Ndebele maxim umuntu ngumuntu ngabantu means “a person is a person through other persons.” Ubuntu, a word shared by Nguni languages such as Zulu, Xhosa and Ndebele, names the moral quality of being a person in the full sense. The philosopher Mogobe Ramose defined it as humaneness.

cards.headline: Personhood is earned
cards.body: Thaddeus Metz reads the maxim as saying your identity as a human being depends, causally and even metaphysically, on community. The Nigerian philosopher Ifeanyi Menkiti argued in 1984 that personhood has to be attained, as you take part in communal life and carry out your obligations. In Akan, a persistently cruel person may be called “not a person”, while still counted a human being.

cards.headline: Tutu’s version
cards.body: Desmond Tutu, who chaired South Africa’s Truth and Reconciliation Commission, carried ubuntu far beyond the seminar room. In No Future Without Forgiveness (1999), he called it “the single main ingredient” that made the commission’s achievements possible.

cards.headline: Where’s the individual?
cards.body: Not everyone accepts the strong version. Michael Onyebuchi Eze criticizes writers who glorify community over the individual and romanticize the past. The individual and the community, he argues, are “not radically opposed”: each forms the other at the same time.

cards.headline: A Person Through Other People: the big picture
learned: Umuntu ngumuntu ngabantu: a person through other persons
Menkiti: personhood is attained, not given
Tutu took ubuntu into public life
Eze: individual and community form each other

questions.prompt: What does the maxim umuntu ngumuntu ngabantu mean?

options.label: A person is a person through other persons
A person is whatever they remember
A person is a name for changing parts
A person first exists, then defines themselves

questions.explanation: The Zulu and Ndebele maxim says a person is a person through other persons.

questions.prompt: On Menkiti’s view, how does someone become a person in the full sense?

options.label: Simply by being born a human being
options.rationale: He says personhood has to be attained.

options.label: By withdrawing from others to think alone
By taking part in communal life
By remembering their own past actions

questions.explanation: Menkiti argued that personhood is attained as one takes part in communal life and carries out one’s obligations.

questions.prompt: Confucius’s junzi in Level 6 is earned, not inherited. What does Menkiti’s ubuntu view share with it?

options.label: Both define a full person by their noble birth
options.rationale: That’s the view Confucius moved away from.

options.label: Both say the self is only a name for parts
Both say that memory is what makes a person
Both treat full personhood as earned by how you live

questions.explanation: Confucius made the junzi a title of moral nobility you earn; Menkiti says personhood is attained through communal life.
